fn:simulation/codemap/server.py::App.dra.explain: At shutdown, handles the messages still waiting in the UDP socket (for at most 1 s) and then sends and records the last batch of calls, so the calls of the final ~200 ms of a short demo, right before demo_traced.sh stops the server, still reach the recording.

fn:simulation/codemap/server.py::App.wri.explain: At shutdown with --record, saves the last /health answer, with EVERY call it could not place (not only the busiest 50) and 'final': true, as <recording name>.health.json next to the recording, and prints a one-line summary. The name does not end in .jsonl, so it is never listed as a recording. Any error just returns None: the shutdown must finish.

fn:simulation/codemap/server.py::Handler.explain: Lets a page opened as a local file (Origin 'null') or from another localhost port read the server's data, by sending Access-Control-Allow-Origin for exactly those origins (nothing for any other website).
Serves any other file of the web folder (for example the sample files), with a guessed content type. A path that would leave the web folder ('..') or a missing file gets 404.

Serves GET /events, the live stream (Server-Sent Events). It takes a place among the at most 8 pages (else 503 'Too many live code map pages are open'), sends 'retry: 2000' and the newest list of running programs right away, then writes every chunk the hub publishes ('event: calls' / 'event: procs'), with a keep-alive comment every 15 s when nothing happens, until the page closes or the server stops.

mod:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace.explain: The live call counter inside every traced Python program. When sitecustomize.py calls install() (only with ASTRA_TRACE=1), it registers a tiny profiler function with Python (sys.setprofile and threading.setprofile) that Python calls at every function start. For a function of the team repo it adds 1 to a counter; everything else is rejected at once. A background thread sends the new counts at most every 100 ms as one small non-blocking UDP message to server.py (127.0.0.1:8091), and a last one when the program ends. It never waits for the network, catches its own errors, skips MAVProxy by default (ASTRA_TRACE_SKIP) and never counts the code map's own files.
mod:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace.effects: UDP datagrams {"pid", "proc", "calls": [[module, file, first line, name, count], ...]} to ASTRA_TRACE_ADDR (default 127.0.0.1:8091)
mod:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace.how_it_fits: Only the simulator switches it on (demo_traced.sh puts simulation/codemap/trace on PYTHONPATH with ASTRA_TRACE=1); nothing on the real drone sets ASTRA_TRACE. Its header lists the measured cost and the exact limits (programs run slower; 1 frame less of Python's recursion limit). test/test_live.py tests it.

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: Finds the repository this tracer file belongs to: the folder three levels above <repo>/simulation/codemap/trace. If the tracer is NOT at that place (a loose copy in /tmp/trace) it gives None, and it never returns '/' or a drive root, because that would make every file of the computer count as team code.
Writes a path in the one spelling used for every comparison: the real path (links followed), the operating system's normal letter case, and '/' separators.
The same as _norm, with exactly one '/' at the end, so the folder '/a/b' never matches a file in '/a/bc/'.

The folders whose files count when ASTRA_TRACE_ROOTS is not set: the repo this tracer lives in (when it is at its proper place) and the Linux-side copy ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026, without duplicates.

The names this program goes by, to compare with ASTRA_TRACE_SKIP: the file name of the program (mavproxy.py), or for 'python -m <module>' the module, which on Linux is read from /proc/self/cmdline because Python has not filled it in yet when sitecustomize runs. 'python -c' gives no name.
Checks whether this program is listed in ASTRA_TRACE_SKIP (default 'mavproxy.py,mavproxy'; '' traces every program), comparing without letter case and with or without '.py'.
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..outputs: the matching program name, or '' when this program should be traced

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: Decides, once per file, whether a file Python runs is team code: not for Python's own '<...>' code, not for this tracer or any simulation/codemap/ file, yes when its real path (colcon's symlinks followed back to ros2_ws/src) starts with one of the roots, or, with the default roots, contains a folder named ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026 (which covers the Windows checkout too).
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..outputs: the real path when it is ours, else None

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: The slow path, run once for each new piece of code: is its file ours (_decide, remembered both ways)? If yes, the first time also starts the sending thread. Code named '<module>', '<lambda>', '<listcomp>' and the like is marked -1 (ours but not a map function, never counted again); a real function gets its report data (module name, real path, first line, name) and its first count. It catches every Exception, so an odd file name can never reach the program.

Builds the profiler function Python calls at every function start (the hot path, kept tiny): it ignores everything but 'call' events, rejects code from known foreign files at once, counts our known functions, and hands brand-new code to _first_call. The whole body sits inside a try that catches only RecursionError and MemoryError, the two errors it can cause itself; an exception the program's own signal handler raises is never swallowed.
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..inputs: the not-ours set, the counts table and the slow-path function (kept as closure variables, the fastest look-up Python has)

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: Reads the send address: 'HOST:PORT' or '[IPv6 address]:PORT' -> (host, port). An empty host, a missing or out-of-range port raises ValueError.
True when the host is an IP address written in numbers (IPv4 or IPv6), so no name look-up (DNS) is needed to send to it.

Makes, on first use, the non-blocking UDP socket and the resolved target address, and keeps them. A bad address (nonsense, port 0, an unknown host) is remembered: counts are then simply dropped. At program exit it refuses a host name that would need a DNS answer, so a program never waits while ending.

Makes the readable process name sent with every message, once: the program's file name ('python -c' / 'python -m' / for 'python3 -m pytest' the package name), plus '(node <name>)' when a ROS 2 node name is given with '__node:='. The server shows it in /health.

Sends the waiting counts as JSON datagrams {'pid', 'proc', 'calls': [[module, file, first line, name, count], ...]}, split so each stays under about 60 kB and at most 8 per flush (the rest waits for the next flush). A message that cannot go at once (busy socket, nobody listening) is dropped and counted, never retried; either way the counts are marked as reported, so nothing piles up.

Collects every function whose count grew since it was last reported and sends the differences with _send. Only one flush runs at a time: it waits for another running flush at most 'wait' seconds (normally not at all) and never waits for the network. It catches every Exception.
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..inputs: wait: seconds to wait for a running flush; at_exit: True during program exit (no DNS look-ups)

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: The background sending thread: sleeps 100 ms (FLUSH_SECONDS) and flushes, again and again, for as long as the program lives. That is how the 'at most one message per process every 100 ms' rule of the contract is kept.

Starts the background sending thread once, and only in programs that actually run team code. It is a raw _thread (not threading.Thread): it starts at once, is never waited for at exit, and does not get the profiler, so it never counts itself.
Registered with atexit: when the program ends, sends what the last 100 ms counted (waiting at most 0.25 s for a running flush), otherwise a short program would report nothing.

After os.fork() without exec, the child process starts fresh: new lock, new socket, new pid and name, no sending thread inherited, and the counts so far marked as already reported (the parent reports those), so each process reports only its own calls. It starts its own sending thread if it runs team code.

Switches tracing on for this program: unless the program is in ASTRA_TRACE_SKIP, it sets the roots (ASTRA_TRACE_ROOTS, else the default roots plus the repo-folder-name rule), excludes the tracer and every simulation/codemap/ folder, sets the send address (ASTRA_TRACE_ADDR, default 127.0.0.1:8091), installs the profiler for this thread and every thread started later, and registers the exit flush and the fork handler. It catches every Exception.
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..called_when: by sitecustomize.py at Python start-up, only when ASTRA_TRACE is exactly 1
fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..outputs: True when installed (or already installed), False when skipped or failed

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: Switches the profiler off for this thread and for threads started later (tests and benchmarks use it); threads already running keep theirs.
Sends the waiting counts right away, waiting at most 0.5 s for a flush already running (for tests and tools).

A small summary of what the tracer has seen, for tests and debugging: installed or not, the skipped program name, the roots, how many files were found ours and not ours, how many functions and calls were counted, datagrams sent and dropped, whether the address was bad and whether the sending thread started.

mod:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace.explain: The live function counter for the simulator's bash scripts. It is sourced only when ASTRA_TRACE=1, by a 3-line hook in simulation/scripts/_common.sh. It uses bash's 'set -T' and a DEBUG trap (a command bash runs before every command) to notice when a function of a team-repo script is entered, counts it per process, and sends the counts to server.py as {'pid', 'sh': script path, 'calls': [[function, count], ...]} over UDP (bash's /dev/udp), at most once every 100 ms per process, right before 'exec', and at exit. Every command it runs is guarded, its trap always returns 0 and keeps $? and PIPESTATUS, and it never replaces an EXIT or DEBUG trap the script already has.
mod:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace.how_it_fits: The bash half of the live map (astra_trace.py is the Python half). Without ASTRA_TRACE=1 this file is never read. Its cost per command and per call is measured in simulation/codemap/README.md.

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/astra_trace..explain: True when an absolute script path belongs to the team repo: it starts with one of the roots, or (with the default roots) contains the repo folder's name. Files under simulation/codemap/ (the code map tools themselves) never count.

Works out '.' and '..' in an absolute path as text only (the file is not touched) and puts the result in _ASTRA_TR_E: '/repo/simulation/scripts/../../../x/lib.sh' becomes '/x/lib.sh'. Without it, a file outside the repo sourced through '..' would look as if it were inside.

Escapes a text for use inside a JSON string (backslash, double quote, newline, carriage return, tab) with bash's own text replacement only, no extra program, and puts the result in _ASTRA_TR_E instead of printing it (printing would need a $( ) subshell for every call).

mod:simulation/codemap/trace/sitecustomi.explain: The on/off switch of the Python tracer. Python runs the first file named sitecustomize it finds on its search path at every start, before the program's own code; with simulation/codemap/trace at the front of PYTHONPATH that is this file. It first runs the system's own sitecustomize that it hides (on Ubuntu the crash-reporter 'apport' hook), so Python behaves exactly as before, and then, ONLY when ASTRA_TRACE is exactly '1', imports astra_trace and calls install(). Without it nothing else happens: no imports, no threads, no profiler, no network. Both steps are inside try/except.
mod:simulation/codemap/trace/sitecustomi.how_it_fits: demo_traced.sh (and the 'export' line of demo_traced.sh --map-only) put this folder on PYTHONPATH with ASTRA_TRACE=1; nothing on the real drone does.

fn:simulation/codemap/trace/sitecustomiz.explain: Runs the next 'sitecustomize' on Python's search path, the one this file hides, exactly like Python's site.py would: normally a plain sitecustomize.py file, which it compiles and runs as a module; in rare cases a sitecustomize package or a compiled .pyc, which it lets the import system load. It never runs itself twice and costs only a few file checks at start-up. If that hidden file fails, the caller prints the same one-line message Python would print.

mod:simulation/codemap/build_artifact.py.explain: Makes ONE shareable file, simulation/codemap/dist/astra_code_map.html, that shows the code map with one recorded simulator run inside and needs no server: it takes web/index.html, removes the outer <!doctype>/<html>/<head>/<body> tags (a Claude artifact adds its own frame), and puts codemap.json and the recording in as window.ASTRA_CODEMAP and window.ASTRA_TRACE, right before the page's own script. It keeps the page at or under 15 MB (15,000,000 bytes, below the artifact limit of 16 MB): the recording is downsampled first (call totals kept exactly), then the source code in the map is reduced step by step.
mod:simulation/codemap/build_artifact.py.how_it_fits: Run after extract.py: 'python3 simulation/codemap/build_artifact.py' (newest recording of recordings/ and ~/.astra_sim/codemap/recordings) or with --recording FILE. The result is published as a Claude artifact; when the page sees the embedded data it makes no network calls at all except its fonts and its layout library. test/test_build_artifact.py tests it.

fn:simulation/codemap/build_artifact.py:.explain: The error for something the person has to fix: a missing file, a code map without blocks, a page missing its embed marker or loading from a host an artifact cannot reach, or a page that cannot be made small enough. main() prints its message and exits with code 2.

Removes the outer page tags (<!doctype>, <html>, <head>, <body>, and the charset and viewport <meta> lines that the artifact frame already has) from web/index.html, but leaves comments, <script> and <style> blocks exactly as they are, even when their text mentions those tags.

Writes data as compact JSON that is safe inside a <script> block: every '<' becomes \u003c (so a text such as '</script>' inside the code map can never end the block early) and the two JavaScript line-separator characters are escaped too.

Checks every src="http..." and href="http..." of the page: each must point at a host a Claude artifact may load from (cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com, fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com). Any other host stops the build with a BuildError naming the addresses.

Turns one recorded line into a clean event, with the same rules as the page's own normalizeEvent: {'event': 'calls', 't', 'calls': {id: count}} (lists of [id, count] are merged, zero or broken counts dropped), {'event': 'procs', 't', 'running': [ids]}, or {'event': 'meta', 'note'}. A line without a usable time, or with nothing in it, gives None and is skipped.
Adds up the call events of every 'window' seconds into one event, stamped with the time of the first event in that window, so a long recording becomes fewer, bigger events with the same totals.

Makes a recording small enough for the page while keeping every function's call total exactly: the running-program lists are kept only when they change (and at least every 30 s, so jumping in the replay finds one), and the call events are merged into windows of 0.4, 0.8, 1.6, 3.2 s ... until at most max_events (3000) events and max_bytes (3 MB) of JSON remain, or the window reaches 120 s. Only the timing gets coarser.

Makes a copy of the code map for one size stage, never changing the original: the trace_index is always dropped (only server.py needs it); 'no-module-source' drops whole-file source, 'short-source' also cuts function source to 60 lines, 'no-source' drops all source, 'no-source-no-doc' also drops the docstring of every function or class that has a plain explanation. It records the stage and whether the source is full, partial or dropped under 'artifact' (the page shows it).

Puts the page together: strips the outer tags, checks the outside addresses and that the <title> is in the first 8 KB (the artifact gallery reads only that), then tries the size stages from 'full' down (each stage's JSON is made once) with the downsampled recording; the first page at or under max_bytes wins and gets build facts (time, recording name, window, event counts). If nothing fits it halves the recording budget (down to 200 events) and tries again, and finally raises BuildError with the smallest size reached.
